# <span id="aanchor85"></span> Master Characteristics

[&lt;&lt; Back](Master%20Characteristics.md#Tabs) \| [Characteristic](Master%20Characteristics%20-%20Characteristic%20Tab.md) \| [Analysis](Master%20Characteristics%20-%20Analysis%20Tab.md) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Contractual/Operational</a>

## Contractual/Operational Tabs

Contractual limits are regulatory requirements defined in a tariff and/or operational agreements, maintenance agreements, and standard operating procedures and include items such as test frequency and sample frequency. These limits can be used to define correction limits, test and sample frequencies for meters, and PPA thresholds.

Operational limits represent limits set by the actual operation of the meter, which may or may not match Contractual limits. Operational limits can be validated against contractual limits to ensure operations meet or exceed contractual limits.

The record has an effective date and an effective end date, but these data points are not used. These records are for all of time. When a new record is created, these fields will be populated with the start and end of time. These values are not editable.

Contractual limits can be manually entered from the Master Characteristics screen or imported from a tab-delimited file (contact <a href="mailto:flowcal.support@quorumsoftware.com" class="notelink">Customer Support</a> to obtain the file format). See also: [Import Contractual Limits](../../Imports/Import%20Contractual%20Limits.md)

<div class="procedure">

To add contractual or operational limits:

1.  Select the **Contractual** or **Operational** tab and click **New**.
2.  Update fields of interest.
3.  Click **OK** to save.

</div>

**Copy Data Button** - Copy the contractual limits to the operational limits.

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Schedule">

The Schedule tab allows you to define frequencies for tests, samples and gravity tests. Each of these fields are validations that are run between meter tasks. You can set the maximum amount of time, the first month of test, sample or gravity test, and the tiering options to schedule tasks if volume reaches certain time-based thresholds. If any of these limits are exceeded an exception will be thrown to notify you that a new task should be scheduled.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 529;height: 738;" />

#### Schedule Sub-Tab Details

The following items are available on the Schedule sub-tab:

- **Test Frequency** - The Test Frequency defines how often the meter should be tested for accuracy.

- **Sample Frequency** - Sample Frequency defines how often a gas stream should have a sample analyzed.

  The last three fields (Accumulated Vol Between Proves, Maximum Time Between Proves, and Meter Factor Change Between Proves) on the Schedules tab are for liquids. Each of these fields are validations that are run between proves. A user can set the maximum amount of volume, maximum amount of time and maximum delta for the meter factor between proves. If any of these fields go above what is set between proves, then an exception will be generated to alert the user.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Sample">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Sample Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Sample">

The Sample tab allows you to store a set analysis for the meter. This analysis can then be used as a reference when working elsewhere in FLOWCAL.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 542;height: 754;" />

#### Sample Sub-Tab Details

The following items are available on the Sample sub-tab:

- **Methane (% of Ethane)** - This limit is only applicable to liquid meters. If you have a contractual limit for methane (C1) as a percentage of ethane (C2), you would enter that limit here. When an analysis is applied to liquid meters, FLOWCAL will calculate component volume values. If the component volume for methane exceeds this limit, the amount of methane over the limit, in gallons, will be stored in excess_c1 in FC_BATCH_REPORT and FC_BATCH_TOTAL. If the limit is exceeded, this value will be displayed on the batch ticket report in the comments section.
- **Carbon Dioxide (% of Ethane)** - This limit is only applicable to liquid meters. If you have a contractual limit for Carbon Dioxide (CO2) as a percentage of ethane (C2), you would enter that limit here. When an analysis is applied to liquid meters, FLOWCAL will calculate component volume values. If the component volume for carbon dioxide exceeds this limit, the amount of carbon dioxide over the limit, in gallons, will be stored in excess_co2 in FC_BATCH_REPORT and FC_BATCH_TOTAL. If the limit is exceeded, this value will be displayed on the batch ticket report in the comments section.

</div>

#### Thresholds Sub-Tab Details

##### Calibration Adjustment

The first four fields (Correction Time Limit (days), Calibration Adjustment Rule, Min Calibration Adjustment Pct, and Min Calibration Adjustment Unit Diff) define test report correction limits used with TESTit Integrated.

Requires TESTit Integrated.

##### PPA Thresholds

The fields in the PPA Thresholds group allow users to set thresholds for PPAs performed on the selected meter. If the threshold criteria is not met, the PPA is automatically rejected and a meter message is generated. The rejected PPA can then be manually unrejected and then approved from the [Edit Approvals](../../Edit%20Approvals/Edit%20Approvals.md) screen.

FLOWCAL gives priority to operational limits. If the operational limits are null, the contractual limit will be enforced. If the operational and contractual Limits are both null, the system limits will be enforced.

FLOWCAL will enforce the same limit type for all data points.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

A user only sets an Operational Limit for Gas Volume and leaves the other data points as null. FLOWCAL will not consider Contractual or System thresholds for the remaining data points since it already encountered an Operational Limit for Gas Volume.

</div>

- **Max PPA Time Frame (Months)** - Maximum time frame beyond which PPAs will be automatically rejected. For example, If the threshold is set to 6 months and in August 2018 a PPA is made to the closed production month of January 2018, the PPA will be auto-rejected since the difference between the production month and current business month is 7 months, which is greater than the threshold.

- **Gas Data Point Thresholds** - Gas meter minimum thresholds for PPAs. When one or more PPA amounts do not exceed the minimums, the PPA will be automatically rejected and a meter message (number 705) will be written. The rejected PPA can be manually unrejected and then approved from the Edit Approvals window (Review \> Approvals). FLOWCAL will first look to see if Operational thresholds have been set. If none are set, then Contractual thresholds will be examined. Finally, if no meter-level thresholds have been set, then system-level thresholds will be examined. Only threshold values for Gas Volume or Energy will be considered for gas meters.

  VCF edits, which are sometimes used to correct data values shown on final reports, do not alter volume but are still saved as PPAs. Such PPAs will be automatically rejected if the thresholds have been set and will need special attention by the user.

- **Liquid Data Point Thresholds** - Liquid meter minimum thresholds for PPAs. When one or more PPA amounts do not exceed the minimums, the PPA will be automatically rejected and a meter message (number 705) will be written. The rejected PPA can be manually unrejected and then approved from the Edit Approvals window (Review \> Approvals). FLOWCAL will first look to see if Operational thresholds have been set. If none are set, then Contractual thresholds will be examined. Finally, if no meter-level thresholds have been set, then system-level thresholds will be examined. Only threshold values for Mass, GSV, or Summed Volume will be considered for liquid meters.

  CF edits, which are sometimes used to correct data values shown on final reports, do not alter volume or mass but are still saved as PPAs. Such PPAs will be automatically rejected if the thresholds have been set and will need special attention by the user.  
    
  The thresholds will only be enforced if the Approval Required PPA Option is selected in System Configuration.

</div>
